one_star_reviews.text: A place with a total lack of empathy and also a lack of professionalism in customer service.
Terrible service and not at all punctual.

*Very poor service
I went to register some documents and the service was very poor.
As soon as I sat down, before I could even speak, the registration clerk rudely asked me, "What do you need?" I wanted to show her the documents, but without letting me explain, she cut me off, saying, "Don't explain anything, they're SEPE papers and we're SOC, I have to call and make another appointment."

I tried to explain the reason for my visit, but she wouldn't let me speak at any point; she was the only one talking. Finally, she saw it was a registration appeal form.
She went to ask if she could register it, and when she came back, she said, "I don't know who helped you write the appeal letter!"

Because it was well-written, as if being a foreigner meant I couldn't write it.
*I felt she was provoking me the whole time, even though I remained calm.* Finally, she registered the appeal form.

*I felt she was provoking me the entire time, even though I remained calm.*
*In the end, she registered the appeal form.* I had to tell her that the receipt was missing from the scan, and she looked angry at me.
Furthermore, she seemed not to know how to scan it again and had to ask two colleagues for help, asking them how to scan another page, and claiming that I hadn't mentioned it at first, when in reality she hadn't even let me speak.*
I was in shock. Unprofessional treatment for a public service.

one_star_reviews.text:
A rather unpleasant experience at Druni. They make you feel constantly watched, and in a very unsubtle way, to the point of being uncomfortable. The most paradoxical thing is that there were more staff members focused on monitoring customers than on serving them, with only one cashier while a huge queue formed. Seeing the situation, we left what we had and went straight to Sephora.

I even felt sorry for one of the employees, because from turning around so much to check on customers, it seemed like she was going to strain her neck with her stares. I think security is important, but a company should also prioritize customer service and comfort.

At Primor, for example, I've never had this feeling. I go into Druni regularly, usually to accompany a friend, but after this experience, we prefer not to shop there again.

one_star_reviews.text:
Extremely disappointing experience and completely unacceptable behavior

I recently purchased a suitcase for around €90 at the Paco Martínez store in FAN Mallorca Shopping. I asked the sales assistant to process the tax refund, as I was eligible for it.

She tried once with my passport and told me it was not possible. I explained that I had just successfully processed a tax refund at Primark using the exact same passport, so I asked her to try again. After around 30 minutes, she finally managed to process it and handed me the document.

Unfortunately, the worst part happened afterwards. In front of me, she turned to her colleague and made a mocking comment, telling her to look at my Louis Vuitton wallet because I was going to “get back €2.”

I find this behavior absolutely disgraceful and completely disrespectful towards a customer. The issue is obviously not the €2 tax refund. The issue is the attitude, mockery and complete lack of professionalism.

I cannot understand how employees can openly make fun of a customer standing right in front of them, apparently thinking that the customer does not understand what they are saying.

I came into the store to make a simple purchase and left feeling extremely uncomfortable and disrespected.

I sincerely hope that Paco Martínez management sees this review and addresses this behavior with the staff. Customers deserve to be treated with basic respect, regardless of how much they spend.

one_star_reviews.text:
A complete sense of abandonment by the Cabanas Town Hall

The feeling of abandonment in Cabanas is deplorable. It seems that the residents' basic needs are not receiving the attention they deserve.

Problems with the water supply and facilities, garbage collection that needs improvement, and roads and pathways that require maintenance and repair are just some examples of a situation that has been ongoing for some time.

This isn't about asking for luxuries, but about demanding decent public services and adequate infrastructure. We, the residents, pay our taxes and have the right to have the necessary resources invested and managed to keep the municipality in good condition.

It is especially frustrating to see that years go by without sufficient improvement in such basic aspects. Cabanas needs more attention, more maintenance, and, above all, for the Town Hall to listen to its residents and take action.

The feeling that remains is one of complete abandonment.

I am very disappointed with the management and lack of empathy of this practice. I enrolled my teenager at this center seeking help at a time when he was feeling very demotivated and discouraged with his studies. As a requirement, I paid €228 upfront and in cash, trusting the psychotherapist, without thinking to ask for a receipt because I felt overwhelmed.

Unfortunately, due to his own state of discouragement, he didn't feel up to attending the sessions. When I requested a refund for the missed sessions (45 minutes per week), the psychotherapist flatly refused to reimburse us without offering any options or solutions. Her justification was that she had already reserved that time in her schedule.

I believe that a mental health professional, especially one who works with teenagers, should show greater understanding, flexibility, and empathy in such a delicate situation. I feel cheated.

one_star_reviews.text: I went to that center sent by my insurance company for rehabilitation after a traffic accident; the doctor had prescribed 15 physiotherapy sessions for me. On the first day, they gave me five appointments in a row. I mentioned that usually when I go to a physiotherapist, we space out the sessions to two per week to recover. He said that's how they did it there, all back-to-back so they could discharge me quickly, so my recovery didn't seem to matter much to him. The problem came later. In the first session, I thought it was strange that he gave me the "massage" with only one hand, but I thought it was just "his technique." The second day I got a little suspicious because it was like when my two-year-old daughter puts lotion on me... and also with only one hand. And on the third day, I realized he was only using one hand because he had his phone with the other. I don't want to think the worst, but I don't know what he was doing with it. I didn't go back (obviously), and I don't recommend anyone go to this center. By the way, I've attached a photo of the state of the pillow I had to put under my belly... I don't know when it was last washed (if it was ever washed at all).

one_star_reviews.text:
What a shameless town! What a fine! 905 euros! NINE HUNDRED EUROS!!!! They slapped me with this for seriously damaging the environment. I drove down a track with the barrier open—I didn't see the "no entry" sign—going 30 km/h, but in open mountain terrain, not in the middle of a forest or anything. My car had a green sticker! A very serious offense, more serious than drunk driving, more serious than hitting a pedestrian...etc. They can shove their town where the sun don't shine.

I haven't thrown away a single piece of aluminum foil, a soda can, any kind of paper, etc., in my life, much less in the mountains. And thanks to my wife, we go to the mountains quite often—the French, Catalan, and Aragonese Pyrenees, to name a few—and they tell me I'm seriously damaging the environment!!!! NINE HUNDRED EUROS!!!!
I will never, ever return to that cursed town. NINE HUNDRED EUROS!!!!

one_star_reviews.text: This experience was a real disgrace. We were scammed out of a €300 deposit and €1400 for a month for my son to stay in a shared apartment. We explained my son's situation and they said he was constantly accompanied by someone who didn't leave him alone for a minute. On the second day, he asked someone for their phone and called his girlfriend from the supermarket. On the third day, they left him sleeping alone because he was taking medication, and everyone went to the gym. He got up and left, only to reappear the next day. He came back and left again for half an hour, then left for a week. He wanted to return to continue his stay, and they told us... We had to pay another €1400 when he still had 20 days left in the month. In short, they threw him away. When he arrived, they didn't register him because we told them not to, and then this Lurdes woman came by, and to top it off, she didn't even give us the contract. I demanded a refund, just that they charge for the week he'd been there, including travel time, and she's playing dumb. We don't know how my son is; we hope nothing happens to him. That center doesn't have qualified staff for these sick people, and I'm going to prove it, and I won't stop until they shut it down. In fact, it's already been reported to several public bodies. This center is located in Murcia, at 5 Conde de Barcelona Street. We're going all the way. I feel cheated, both financially and, above all, morally. And the worst part is the fear of not knowing how my son is. They are unscrupulous people, but this time they shouldn't continue to harm people who are vulnerable when their child is ill. You'll hear from the law; that's how things get sorted out.

one_star_reviews.text:
A terrible experience. I went to this garage to have a leak in my car checked and get a repair estimate.

I dropped off the car in the morning, and a few hours later, they called to tell me that a whole part needed replacing, with an estimate of €590. Since that seemed excessive, I decided not to have it repaired there and took it to another garage to compare prices.

When I picked up the car that same morning, they told me it had taken them a full hour to locate the source of the leak. I had to pay €60 for the supposed inspection.

A few days later, I took the car to another garage. There, right in front of me and in literally 4-5 minutes, they removed two parts and located the problem. It wasn't necessary to replace the entire part that Autocam had quoted me for (it was in perfect condition). The leak was simply coming from a nearby plastic hose…

Result: €130 for repairs at the other garage, including labor, compared to the €590 Autocam quoted me to replace a part that was fine.

“Fortunately,” I paid €60 for a full HOUR of an INCORRECT diagnosis…

I absolutely do not recommend them. The service was terrible, and they even hung up on me.
Yesterday, I uploaded my resume and created a profile on this temporary employment agency's website. It started giving me problems that I tried to fix, such as not being able to edit my profile, log in from the homepage, or recover my password. Also, despite uploading a resume focused on the hospitality industry, it was offering me jobs as a truck driver or pool installer.
Since I couldn't resolve the issues myself yesterday, I called today. A guy answered the phone with complete indifference and, after telling me another colleague would assist me, left me on hold. As soon as the colleague answered, I explained what had happened with her colleague, and she quickly made excuses instead of taking the situation seriously. I explained what happened yesterday, and she asked me, "But did you apply for a hospitality job in Valencia yesterday?" And I said yes, I'm from there, and now that you mention it, I also noticed an error in the job description. The salary is listed one way in one section and a completely different hourly rate in another. She seemed uninterested in helping me and told me she was going to give me the phone number for the Valencia office so I could tell them about the job posting and they could correct it, since it was their job posting, saying it wasn't their responsibility. Quite confused, I asked her, "But the problem is that I can't access my profile, etc... What does that have to do with different offices? Can't you escalate my problem to the IT department so they can fix it?" She gave an evasive answer, saying they'd never had anything like this happen before, and angrily told me to have a good day and hung up on me. I find this incredibly disrespectful, so unfortunately, I will never recommend this company. It's unbelievable that a job search company would have such unprofessional employees.

one_star_reviews.text:
Disastrous. We called them about a house in my town where we wanted to improve the roof. The house wasn't leaking; we simply wanted to extend the roof's lifespan until we could save up for a future renovation. So we decided to call this company. One of the conditions for them to do the work was that they not cover the skylights in the roof.

To my surprise, they called me saying they had finished the job, and when I asked if they had left the skylights, they told me they had covered them. I don't understand why, since I told them that NOT COVERING the skylights was a non-negotiable condition, they covered them on their own. In the end, they admitted their mistake and went to cut the skylights. I don't know how they did it, but they drilled through the roof. Since then, we've had leaks... they were second-hand, and there are still leaks that weren't there before.

Textbook incompetence, the epitome of it all: they came to waterproof a roof that wasn't leaking and left it riddled with holes.

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience with this health center has changed drastically for the worse. For years I had an excellent family doctor, "Rosa," a truly spectacular professional, and I never had these kinds of problems. Since she retired, I've had two different doctors, and the care, at least in my case, has declined significantly.

On several occasions, I've requested a telephone appointment, and they simply haven't called me back. This means wasting the day waiting for a doctor's call that never comes and having to start all over again with another appointment.
The worst part for me is the waiting time. If I need a doctor to examine me because I'm sick, have a gynecological problem, need a prescription, or, like now, have a sore tonsil, it's no good being given an appointment for about 15 days from now. What am I supposed to do in the meantime?
Due to gynecological problems, I ended up going to private healthcare, paying for consultations, specialists, and medications out of my own pocket. And frankly, it's incredibly frustrating to have to do that when you work and pay into the system precisely to have access to public healthcare when you need it. My last phone appointment, just a few days ago, was the final straw. I felt like the doctor was in a huge rush to end the call. I'd explain a question, "Okay, fine," and it seemed like it was time to hang up. I tried to ask another question, and again, the feeling was that the call had to end as quickly as possible. I had a third question I needed to ask, and in the end, I didn't even bring it up because you reach the point where you feel like you're bothering the doctor or wasting their time.

And honestly, I don't know what the problem is. I don't know if the doctors have impossible schedules, if they're allocated very few minutes per patient, if there's a staff shortage, or if it's simply poor organization at the clinic. I'm not going to blame anyone in particular for something I don't know about. What I can assess is the outcome as a patient, and my experience so far has been very bad.

I'm not asking for immediate attention for every little thing. I'm asking for something as basic as being able to see my primary care physician within a reasonable timeframe, for a phone appointment to actually take place, and to be able to explain what's happening to me without feeling like the conversation has to be ended as soon as possible. After years of receiving excellent care at this same center, it's even more disheartening to see how things have changed. I hope they investigate what's going wrong, because behind every appointment there's a person who may be ill and needs care, not just a number to be removed from the schedule.

one_star_reviews.text:
They're clearly out of their depth when it comes to dealing with the public. They lack manners, education, and professionalism.

The first thing you need to work with the public is good manners, courtesy, and the ability to treat people, not treat them like clowns. And if you're not cut out for customer service, then do something else.

Now, let's talk about the monthly magazines. It seems to cause the owner tremendous stress, and he doesn't understand why we, the users, are interested in them. He even goes so far as to disown the brand and the distributor. Of course, I imagine he's not so bothered about the commission the magazines bring in…

You ask about a magazine, and he treats you rudely: saying it hasn't arrived, that he won't reserve it for you, that nobody told him to reserve it for you… But curiously, when it suits him, he does reserve it for you and even sends you a photo to your phone to mark it as yours. So, what's the deal?

And today was the last straw. Several of us were waiting in case the distributor arrived. You wait there for an hour, and after seeing you waiting all that time, the woman tells you straight up to find another place, that she's not going to sell you that magazine because she's going to sell it to the people who buy it every month… You should have said that from the beginning, but you can't take us for fools. This shows your poor management and organizational skills.

If you have waiting lists that have been going on for weeks, if you don't know how many copies you're going to receive, or if you can't guarantee that a magazine will be available, FINE. You say it from the very beginning: “I have a waiting list, I can't guarantee that I'll get stock, and if it does arrive, we'll see.” Period.

But don't make people wait, don't make them wait an hour, and then, after they've already been there waiting, tell them you're not going to sell it to them.

Like I said: managing this issue is way out of your league, and especially dealing with the public. Lack of professionalism, poor judgment, and worst of all, a truly appalling attitude.

And of course, since they have no competition here in Nava, they can get away with certain things. Because if there were another newsstand nearby, more than a few people would think twice about where to buy their newspapers.

Think about it. It's one thing to be out of stock, but quite another to waste people's time and treat them like they're bothering you just for wanting to buy something.

one_star_reviews.text:
I don't usually leave negative reviews, but this time I think it's more than deserved. Yesterday, I went to the pharmacy with a valid veterinary prescription for medication my cat urgently needs. To expedite the process, my vet sent it to me as a PDF. One of the pharmacists told me they could give it to me given the urgency and the validity of the prescription, and that I should bring the original later. Note: I was going to pick up the medication from the pharmacy on Friday and then bring the prescription first thing Saturday morning. When I went to pick up the medication on Friday, they refused to give it to me because I didn't have the original. I tried to explain what the colleague had told me the day before, but they flatly refused. I have a degree in Pharmacy and have worked in many pharmacies; I know there's no problem with this practice, as long as the original prescription is brought later and is valid. I also know that copies of private prescriptions can be submitted to the Official College of Pharmacists of Madrid (COFM), something that can't be done with prescriptions from the public health system.

I wanted to leave this review not because of the way things were handled, but because of the urgent need for this medication. It's a shame that exceptions are made for some customers even without a prescription, while for others, who aren't regular customers, no exceptions are made even with a prescription.

one_star_reviews.text: They don't allow photos. "It's not a museum," were the exact words of the person who forbade us from taking pictures.

I entered this church with my family, carrying my phone, but I had no intention of taking photos. It's a church I know well, and frankly, I had no need to photograph it. Even so, a man approached me in a very rude manner and said directly, "I don't want any photos."

I still don't know exactly what his role was or what position he held there, but the way he spoke to me was completely unnecessary and very unpleasant. Furthermore, there was no visible sign indicating that photography was prohibited. It's even more striking that he was using his phone and sending messages while reprimanding me for something I wasn't even doing: my phone was turned off.

The church is beautiful, but the experience was truly disappointing. I completely understand that there are rules and that they should be respected, but they can be communicated politely and respectfully. After this experience, it's no surprise that it's usually empty. It's a shame, because the place deserves so much more.

one_star_reviews.text:
I didn't expect to have to give a negative review, but I have no other choice. From July, when I reserved the car, until the end of August, I still didn't have my car, a Hyundai Tucson KXN. At first, they said it needed some bodywork and paint repairs; a mirror was broken, and they still haven't fixed it. Then, when it was finally ready and I went to pick it up, on the way home, the particulate filter warning light came on. I had to take it back, incurring the cost of transport again. To save money, instead of replacing the filter right away, they took it to a garage where they regenerated it. I went to pick up the car again, the warning light came on again, and that same day I had to leave the car. They took it to one garage, and the warranty people said it wasn't valid. They took it to another garage, and that didn't work either. Finally, they took it to yet another garage, and they said they had the part and that I had to get a quote for the replacement and "let's see if the warranty approves it."

I don't know where this is going to end, but I deeply regret going to Ocasión Plus. First and last time I'll go there.

I must say that the service was always good, but there were no solutions.

one_star_reviews.text:
We are absolutely disappointed with this hospital. We were regular patients through Axa insurance and have received good service for the past few years. There are three of us at home, and we always made sure when booking appointments by phone that we would be seen by doctors who work with Axa.

A few days ago, we made a phone appointment for my wife, explicitly stating that we are Axa policyholders, as we always do, and we were given an appointment with a doctor. Most hospitals logically tell you which doctors accept insurance when you call.
When we arrived at reception, we asked when they would accept our insurance card, but they told us, "Not at the moment, go and the nurse will tell you" (their exact words). After the appointment, they charged us 250 euros. It turns out the doctor wasn't an Axa doctor. What a shock!
We paid and filled out a complaint form, which we believe is useless. (No response)
We complained, but they completely washed their hands of it, claiming that the doctor doesn't work with AXA and that it's our fault for not mentioning that we were with AXA.
In the 30 years we've had the insurance, since it was Winterthur, this has never happened to us in any hospital.
We won't be going back, and I think that's a significant loss for the hospital. Those of you who use insurance should be very careful.

At our appointment a week ago, the psychiatrist told us to call her with any questions or concerns.
We have a small question about the medication adjustment, and there's no way to get through on the phone. I've been calling continuously for two days.
This is shameful.

I call and they hang up on me. They've stopped my psychiatric medication without any warning, and I haven't been able to buy it for over three days. As is well known, abruptly stopping medication is considered dangerous for the patient. Right now, I'm very distressed because of the lack of medication, and I've moved to a different province, so the only way to contact them is by phone, and they don't even answer, even though I called during the center's opening hours.
This is irresponsible; they're putting people's health at risk. I gave it one star because I can't give it less.
Shameful service, good professionals but long waiting lists and they don't even answer the phone.

You go to the clinic with an appointment scheduled for your child back in June. You arrive, they take your information, and after sitting in the waiting room for 50 minutes... you go to the reception desk to ask about your appointment, and they tell you that you've missed it and to come back in three weeks. Completely unprofessional and shameless.

I've been calling every day for a week, several times throughout the morning, and there's no way to get through to them! Ugh! And then you reschedule your appointment because you can't make it, and they give you the next one for six months later. It's shameful!

one_star_reviews.text: Meloko.art cc granaita. The saleswoman was incredibly rude and gave me a bad attitude. She even tried to scam me. Since you buy something for a certain price, if it doesn't fit, they don't give you a refund. You choose something else that costs less, for example, a pendant with an interchangeable chain, and for whatever reason, it's too short, so you exchange it for a longer one. If the chain is cheaper than the one I'm exchanging, I'd have money left over, and now I can exchange the chain for a longer one that they tell me costs €20 just for the chain. If the pendant already costs X with a slightly longer chain, I understand it might cost a little more, but on top of what I paid for the exchange, I have to pay another €13 when the new item is supposed to be cheaper, and I have money in my favor. I should only have to pay the difference between the price of the pendant with the slightly longer chain. I don't understand why I ended up paying €13 more for the product compared to the one I replaced, even though the slightly smaller chain costs less than the one I replaced and it's just a matter of putting on a larger one. In conclusion, don't go there because they don't give good advice either. They just ask you questions and tell you, "We have this and this, whichever you like." They don't even offer advice or their opinion, nothing.

Excellent in every respect, could not have been better.
The above was after our first visit when we gave it five stars.
Further to this, my wife broke her tooth on Thursday the 16th July, she called into the practice on Friday the 17th to see if she could get an Emergency appointment as we were leaving for the UK on Saturday the 18th, and as we are Spanish residents, and have been for nearly 10 years do not have a dentist in the UK. They gave her an appointment for Thursday the 3rd September after we had returned. On the evening of the 2nd she received a message that due to unforseen family problems this had been cancelled and a new appointment had been made for the 6th October. This would be nearly three months since she first tried to get an emergency appointment . She messaged back and asked for an earlier one and was told if she didn't like it then go to another dentist or even return to the UK. Yes we will be going to another dentist and NOT going back to the UK.
Dra Susanna is a excellent dentist and a lovely person but you cannot treat your patients like this.

one_star_reviews.text:
We are currently on the bus for the Teide excursion and would like to express our great disappointment regarding the way this service was sold to us.
When we purchased the excursion, your salesperson presented it to us as a simple round trip to Teide with the cable car, telling us that it would only take the morning. At no point were we informed that it was actually a full tour of Teide, an excursion we had already done before by buggy.
We were also never informed that a meal was included, nor were we told about the possibility of the cable car being closed or cancelled due to weather conditions.
We paid €160 for two people, which we already considered quite expensive for what we believed was simply a return bus journey with a cable car ride. We are now discovering that the service we were sold is completely different from what was presented to us.
The most problematic part is that we had already booked and paid for a boat excursion this afternoon, which we will now be unable to attend because the Teide excursion actually lasts the entire day.
We therefore genuinely feel that the salesperson was primarily interested in selling us the most expensive package possible, without providing the essential information we needed to make an informed decision.
We would nevertheless like to point out that the staff on the bus have been extremely helpful, professional and welcoming. Our dissatisfaction concerns only the way in which the excursion was sold to us.
The company’s response to this complaint was simply to tell us to deal directly with the salesperson, claiming that they are not responsible for the issue
Their response is quite easy to turn against them: they take the payment and organize the service, but completely distance themselves from the way it is sold.

one_star_reviews.text:
Our experience with Alicia before the first session was not good.

We had a couples therapy appointment scheduled and confirmed in writing. The day before, we received two reminders requesting confirmation, but I was unable to respond due to work commitments. We never canceled the appointment or expressed any doubts about attending. In fact, my partner went to withdraw cash to pay for the session, and I had rearranged my work schedule to be able to attend.

Even so, we received a message first thing on the day of the appointment informing us that it had been canceled due to lack of confirmation. When we explained the situation, we were told that we had doubts about starting therapy, which was untrue. We were also told that responding to a message "takes a moment," without any knowledge of the personal and work circumstances that prevented me from doing so. These two interpretations—assuming we had no intention of attending and taking for granted that it's always possible to respond—seemed inappropriate.

We fully understand that appointments have confirmation procedures and that the work of professionals is important. What bothered us was that, despite prior confirmation and having explained that we simply couldn't respond to the last reminder, our lack of response was interpreted as a lack of interest or doubt about our decision to start therapy.

They eventually offered to keep the session, but after how the situation had unfolded, we preferred not to begin therapy there, as we consider it essential to have trust from the very beginning.

one_star_reviews.text:
*Disastrous Experience and Complete Lack of Trust*

Our experience with InfoKasa, specifically with Marta Céspedes, and with José Enrique Gómez Móndejar of TecniTasa, has been disastrous. Carlos Vegara González, the property owner, was also involved.

We were presented with a property described as urban, mortgageable up to approximately 80%, and with an appraisal practically guaranteed to be above the purchase price. However, during the process, we discovered that the property's zoning status was very different: no other appraiser, bank, or urban planning lawyer we consulted considered the transaction valid under the terms presented to us. In practice, the property turned out to be unmortgageable, classified as rural, and with various defects and problems that had not been initially disclosed to us.

What is particularly serious is that we raised numerous concerns before proceeding, and José of TecniTasa expressly assured us that the appraisal was valid. Subsequently, the other professionals we consulted clearly disagreed with that valuation.

When the purchase fell through, recovering the deposit was a complete nightmare. We felt utterly deceived by the information and guarantees we received. This transaction resulted in financial losses, countless hours of dealing with the issue, and entirely avoidable distress.

We strongly advise any potential buyer not to accept verbal assurances; to request absolutely everything in writing; and to commission an independent review of the Land Registry, Cadastre, City Hall, and zoning regulations by a specialized lawyer before handing over a single euro.

A shameful experience that we wouldn't wish on anyone.

Pain treatment not recommended.

I arrived with quite severe lower back pain, something that happens to me regularly, and my goal this time was very specific: to relieve the pain so I could continue enjoying my vacation.

The physiotherapist is knowledgeable and clearly has expertise in the field, but in my case, I felt the session was too focused on analyzing the origin of the problem, poor posture, and explaining the symptoms, as well as recommending exercises to do at home. All of this can be very useful in a medium- or long-term treatment, but since I was only attending one session while on vacation, my priority was to have the area treated and get pain relief, and I didn't feel that goal was met.

I don't doubt his knowledge or professionalism, but if you're looking for a one-off session focused primarily on relieving specific pain, in my case, it wasn't the experience I was expecting.

one_star_reviews.text: I ordered a squid and they were very hard and rubbery, I asked the waiter and told him about it that these squid could not be eaten and he told me that 5 pieces came out and no one advertised. I told him that mine couldn't be eaten. He took my plate, I waited half an hour, hoping it would bring a soft plate, but I didn't get it. I approach him (please ask for a bill) because I ordered other dishes and he issues me a receipt with squid on it. I ask him to deduct it from my bill and he says to me, "If you don't pay, I call the police." Call him, the police are coming and I had to pay and write a complaint on a special print and now I have to report it if I want to get my money back. I have never seen such service. I felt like I was in a restaurant managed by the mafia. Avoid this place with a wide arc, you will not eat anything good here and if you report a problem, they immediately call the police. The policeman was very nice, he calmly explained everything, but I had to pay and then I can file a complaint with the relevant office. Tourists are treated very badly. I travel all over the world, I've never seen this treatment before in my life. I paid 50 euros for squid, which was not suitable for eating.

one_star_reviews.text: Deceptive advertising. They offer a treatment at one price, and when you go to get it, they tell you that the two sessions you initially paid for are only one, that this session already contains twice the amount of product, and that's why it's reduced to a single dose. You complain, and they don't care. Completely misleading advertising.

⭐️

My experience with Dorsia Burgos has been very negative, and frankly, I'm completely disappointed with how they handled my case. I initially went to the clinic to inquire about surgery. During the first consultation, they gave me some prices, and based on that information, I paid €1,000 as a deposit. However, after making the payment, the person who was assisting me started messaging me on WhatsApp to say that the prices they had initially given me were incorrect and that the actual cost was different. For me, given that it was something important and a considerable amount of money, these constant changes generated enormous distrust and made me lose the confidence I needed to continue with the procedure. For that reason, the next day I informed them that I didn't want to have any procedure done and requested a refund of the €1,000. What worries me most is that, after three months, I'm still waiting for my money back. At the time of payment, I was not clearly informed that the amount was non-refundable, nor was I provided with a signed contract agreeing to the non-refundable terms. I believe that a clinic that works with medical procedures and significant sums of money should offer clear information, accurate prices, and transparent terms from the outset, especially before receiving such a large amount. After three months, I still haven't received my €1,000 back. I find this situation utterly disappointing and feel it's important to share my experience so that others, before handing over any money, request all terms, prices, and any cancellation and refund policies in writing.

I hope Dorsia Burgos will finally resolve this situation and refund my money.
They've had my UPS package for 4 days and they still haven't picked it up.

one_star_reviews.text:
We are publishing this review on the profile of this property, managed by Casuca Norte, because the company does not have its own Google listing where owners can share their experiences.

Our experience as owners with Casuca Norte, in our first rental managed by them this June, has been very negative.

Before publishing this review, we tried every possible way to reach a solution and an understanding with María, both amicably and through a formal complaint, without success.

The guests, who according to María were wonderful guests the previous year, caused damage to the property whose repair costs far exceed the rental amount. After formally requesting that Casuca repair or remedy this damage, María has ignored our claim, despite having already received her commission for the management and the security deposit.

As owners, we have felt completely abandoned, since Casuca collects and manages the security deposit, and in our case, it was not used to cover the damages caused.

Furthermore, although we were assured that the property would be delivered completely clean, only the interior had been cleaned. The entire exterior area was extremely dirty and uncleaned.

This review does not replace the formal actions and claims we have already initiated to defend our rights; it simply aims to inform other homeowners of our experience so they don't suffer the same fate. We entrusted the management of our brand-new, recently occupied property to them and expected the guarantees that were offered, which, in our experience, have not been honored.

one_star_reviews.text: The first time I came here was because of depression related to my work situation. Dr. Paola's response? "I can't put you on sick leave for this. Who's going to work then?" That's exactly what she said. After a month and a half, following a labor conciliation hearing, the company had to compensate me and correct all the hours I worked that hadn't been included in my contract and for which I hadn't received social security contributions. To top it all off, after I left, my boss assaulted one of my colleagues. In other words, my situation was real; I genuinely had problems, and this doctor did what he did to me. This was in 2023. I went to the Netherlands and returned this past July. I came back to this center. They did a blood test. The first time I've ever had a needle stick and it hurt. But oh well, these things happen. The results came back a week later. I arrived at the appointment and the doctor told me she couldn't give me the results on paper because "it's too much trouble," that I had to download "my citizen's folder" and then they asked for an "electronic certificate." I did it. The reports are nowhere to be found. I went to the Netherlands because of this; they're taking away our rights at every turn. The services are getting worse and worse, in healthcare and in general. This is worse than a dictatorship.

Endless waits; both appointments took over an hour. The doctor acted like, "That's not my problem, why are you telling me this? Go downstairs and make an appointment with the other doctor." Healthcare workers arguing amongst themselves in public. Waiting lists of months for urgent tests.

one_star_reviews.text:
We had a terrible experience with Lorena. We took my 10-year-old son to her office because of his fears, and after two sessions with her, and a Star Wars movie that affected him deeply, my son worsened. He began experiencing anxiety, stopped sleeping and eating normally, and had trouble breathing. I told Lorena about this, and she simply said it could be normal after the first few sessions, but if we thought he was getting worse, we could stop going for a while to see if he improved. Instead of taking responsibility for the situation and scheduling an earlier appointment, increasing the frequency, and attending to my son, despite the normal concerns we parents might have, she simply told me not to use her WhatsApp for this. However, she didn't offer any other way to communicate, only the final 15 minutes on the day of the appointment. She didn't give us any guidance or advice on how to help our son, and we felt very alone and lost. We felt no understanding or empathy at any point. Working with families and providing guidance to parents is essential for therapy to be effective.

In the end, we decided to discontinue therapy at this clinic. I informed Lorena, and she simply said, "Very well, I'll cancel the appointment." That's the level of compassion and professionalism she demonstrated.

one_star_reviews.text:
A complete botch job. The renovation they did was riddled with errors:
The bathroom vanity is tilted.
The toilet is crooked relative to the wall and also generates bad odors.
The floors are unlevel.
The ceiling is unfinished.
Many paint defects. It's clear they wanted to save money at the expense of the result.
One of the radiators they installed is leaking.
The water inlet they installed is too low. They had to break the kitchen cabinet to get water in. When removing a window grate, they broke bricks on the facade because they ripped it out completely. They're just incompetent.
The bathroom floor is lower than the rest of the house.
They forgot to install the thermal insulation they had contracted for.
The baseboards are detached. The terrace enclosure is poorly insulated; there's noticeable dampness.
Some electrical outlets protrude from the wall, and most of the outlets are tilted. They acted like they didn't know anything was happening during the construction. A disgrace, and completely unprofessional. Hiring these people was absolutely insane. And don't even bother looking for them afterward, because the owner, whom you'll never see, isn't in Madrid. A total rip-off.

one_star_reviews.text:
Terrible service.
The FNMT (National Mint and Stamp Factory) informed us that we could go there to complete the process (a quick procedure). When we arrived, the clerk, Sarai, sent us to the civil registry to complete the process because, according to her, it wasn't handled at this office. Dissatisfied with her rudeness and ignorance, we decided to go to another area within the same building where, based on previous experience, we knew they did handle it. However, the security guard at the entrance told us not to go there. There, we received excellent service and were told that Sarai was in charge of this procedure. As we were about to return to the original location, the security guard approached us, fuming, saying that we had taken advantage of her distraction to go where she had initially told us not to go. Suddenly, all three security guards were there, greeting us as if we were criminals, unnecessarily imposing their authority since we were only trying to complete our paperwork. They kept repeating that we were being disrespectful by not following their unnecessary authoritarianism, while we tried to explain that the real problem was that Sarai, the official on duty, didn't provide accurate information and didn't even make the slightest effort to resolve the issue. It was an absolute farce that once again demonstrates their complete disregard for the taxpayer.

one_star_reviews.text:
A very bad experience with this laundry service. I work in a hotel, and we receive the laundry in quite poor condition. Sometimes towels and sheets arrive stained or dirty in ways that shouldn't be there, and other times the laundry is poorly ironed.

Furthermore, we've received items from other hotels, and we routinely receive less laundry than we send. Because of this, we have to constantly monitor the quantities, counting everything that goes out and everything that comes back.

We've also had problems with the labeling and identification of the laundry, as the information is often incorrect, which creates even more work and organizational problems.

And when you try to contact them to complain or resolve an issue, they often don't even answer the phone.

For an industrial laundry service that works with hotels, I believe there should be much more organization, control, and responsibility regarding clients' laundry. The experience so far has been quite disappointing.

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience in the Clinical and Biomedical Laboratory Science degree program has been very negative, and I would not recommend this institution.

We were promised lab coats with the logo included in the tuition fees, but they never arrived, and we had to buy them ourselves. The practical placements were also disappointing: in the first year, we were sent to a foundation in Móstoles with limited resources, and we were even told to find our own placements. There was hardly any flexibility to combine them with work, and in the second year, despite having taken the university entrance exam (EVAU), we were again assigned to centers very far away. They even offered placements in pharmacies, which were unrelated to the degree, so some students ended up choosing unsuitable options simply because of their proximity.

Furthermore, basic materials for the practical sessions were lacking. For example, there weren't enough microscope slides, and we had to reuse and clean them, which could affect the quality of the samples.

Regarding the teaching staff, some people didn't seem to have relevant qualifications for the subjects they were teaching. The content was often very generic and focused primarily on memorizing information, with little practical depth. There were also unprofessional situations: faced with complaints about the excessive amount of material, one professor even suggested changes to the assessment. In another instance, a professor repeatedly presented a classmate in front of the entire class, making them present without prior notice, asking them questions about the material, and then demanding assignments with only a day's notice.

The administrative management was also poor. I had to request the money from a scholarship for months before it was finally processed.

The graduation ceremony was also disappointing: we were forced to pay for a photographer whose treatment of some students was quite unpleasant, and whose photographs did not justify the price.

I also found the academic recognition disappointing. One classmate achieved the highest grade across all the programs at the center in Madrid, and, in our experience, received no recognition commensurate with that result.

Finally, the administration constantly encouraged us to leave positive reviews, while their ability to resolve problems seemed quite limited. Currently, I'm also seeing reviews from former classmates being discredited because they claim the students aren't listed as enrolled at the center, even though they were in the same class as me.

In short, I believe the organization, the practical training, the resources, the management, and some of the faculty fall far short of what I expected from a vocational training program. I recommend researching thoroughly and speaking with former students before enrolling.

one_star_reviews.text:
Our experience with the center was a few years ago, and unfortunately, it wasn't satisfactory.

I remember the assessment cost us approximately €800 to €1,000, so we expected a very thorough and personalized report. However, when we received it, it had another child's name on it. When we pointed this out, they simply crossed out the name and wrote the correct one in pen. For the price we paid, this seemed unprofessional.

Furthermore, the report's conclusions were unclear and too vague, presenting different possibilities without sufficiently specifying the child's situation or what steps we should take.

At the same time, the counselor at his school conducted another assessment that we found much more precise and specific, with conclusions that truly helped us understand the situation.

Finally, they offered us treatment with their specialists. Initially, they quoted us €400 per month, but without us having requested any discount or reduction, they offered us €250 per month. The way it was presented made us quite suspicious; frankly, it seemed more like something you'd find at a flea market than a professional center.

Although a few years have passed and conditions may have changed, that was our experience, and for the price we paid, we expected much more rigor, clarity, and professionalism.

I don't know who is behind this, but it's one of the worst services and reputations imaginable.

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience with after-sales service and warranty management has been very disappointing.

I bought the vehicle in March 2016; it was barely two years old and had 18,000 km on the odometer. It has been out of service since August 30th, and after more than a month and a half, I still haven't received a definitive solution.

When I was told that the repair could take several weeks, I had to resort to renting a vehicle to get around, accumulating over €1,000 in expenses. Given the prolonged breakdown and the associated costs, I finally had to lease a vehicle to try to reduce the expense.

I find the lack of a solution that prevents the customer from having to bear such significant financial consequences while their vehicle is out of service and awaiting repairs particularly disappointing.

Currently, the case is being reviewed by a law firm, and I plan to also take it to the relevant consumer protection agencies.

I am sharing my experience so that other buyers can take it into account when evaluating after-sales service and warranty management.

one_star_reviews.text:
Unfortunately, the experience has been negative, both due to the high number of deficiencies that have appeared and, on several occasions, the way they have been handled.

Six months have passed since the completion of the work, and we continue to find consequences of an execution that, in several cases, left much to be desired. The latest example is a crack that has appeared in a bathroom tile, and which, due to its location and the way the cabinet was installed, is directly related to the work carried out.

During the installation, the carpenter forcibly fitted the wooden cabinet door and frame into an opening that did not correspond to its dimensions, even breaking the surrounding plasterboard frame. At that time, I personally warned both the carpenter and the manager about what was happening, but I was assured that it wasn't a problem and that, in their exact words, "fitting the furniture the way he did is completely standard practice."

Time, unfortunately, has proven otherwise.

It wasn't an isolated incident. Something similar happened with the hinges of a door that had been rebated. After the adjustment, damage occurred to the door frame, and the carpenter also denied responsibility for this.

Another particularly significant incident was dampness that appeared four months after the work was completed. When I reported the problem, they initially chose not to respond. Only after I insisted and warned them of the potential liability arising from the work carried out, and that I would send a formal legal notice, did they decide to address the situation. Furthermore, on the first visit, the company's staff and the renovation coordinator arrived without the necessary equipment to locate the source of the leak. Fortunately, my insurance adjuster was present and ultimately located a leak originating from one of the fittings made by the company.

And these are just a few examples. Since the completion of the work, several issues have been identified: paint damaged by dents and marks caused during construction, to which the initial response from the project coordinator, given that it was a freshly painted wall, was that we could use a "magic eraser from Mercadona"; a chipped porcelain tile; an unsealed shower tray; unsealed and unpainted bathroom grout lines; gaps several centimeters from the wall in the upper frames of several doors; a kitchen cabinet door that arrived broken twice and took over a month to replace; and a blind that, once installed, wouldn't even go up or down correctly.

These issues were eventually resolved. Other deficiencies, such as the aforementioned bathroom tile, the hinge, and a door frame that didn't fit perfectly into the wall, will remain as they are.

The most disappointing aspect, therefore, hasn't been the problems that arose during a renovation—something that can happen in any construction project—but rather the accumulation of issues and, above all, the situation, responses, and overall unpleasant feeling it generated.

I don't consider it acceptable that the client has to dedicate so much time and effort to resolving issues that shouldn't even be happening and that are related to the work or repairs they're supposed to fix.

After six months of problems and continuing to find deficiencies related to the renovation, my assessment can only be negative.

one_star_reviews.text:
I got a semi-permanent manicure and a week later, one of my nails chipped. She made an appointment the same day, and when I asked why it happened, she angrily told me it was MY fault, that we don't know how to take care of our nails, that it was the index finger of my right hand and it's the one I use the most... I said I wasn't blaming her, it just seemed strange to me, but anyway, I paid her €2 for the repair, thanked her, and that was that.

But that same night, the nail on the index finger of my other hand chipped again. It was already strange, but I didn't say anything, praying it would hold until September 4th. But four days later, another one on my left hand chipped. I sent her a photo and asked if she could come in. She sent me a voice message saying it was Friday, impossible, and that she could only come on Monday if there were any cancellations. So I called her and asked if I could come in, even just so she could see me, and maybe it was my nail. She said, "Why bother? It's obvious I did it myself." I told her I wasn't blaming her, I just wanted her opinion in case there was another technique to try. She said it wouldn't do any good because she'd already seen them and it was clear it wasn't her fault.

I told her it was a shame to lose a client like that. I was paying the €4, because I never said it was her; it could have been my nail. What's clear is that I've had semi-permanent polish for many years and it's never happened to me before, and I know how to take care of my nails.
I think I was very polite; it was the second time it had broken, and the least I could do was try to fix the problem. And so, I lost a client.
